method: Executed differential against Boost.Regex. An oracle driver outside this repository (../oracle/boost-regex/driver.cpp) was compiled against the header-only Boost.Regex 1.92 and run over a deterministic corpus that ../oracle/boost-regex/gen.py derives from the pinned OpenMS checkout: every Boost.Regex expression the pinned library and class tests use, with source-derived, structured, adversarial (line separators \n \r \r\n \f \v, NUL, non-ASCII and invalid UTF-8 bytes, Arabic-Indic digits, empty inputs) and seeded random inputs, plus syntax probes, the probes of the independent review and of the work bounds (family ADV), and grammar-generated expressions. The driver uses OpenMS's call shapes: basic_regex construction with perl syntax and the icase/no_mod_s flags, regex_search and regex_match into an smatch, named sub-expression lookup, and sregex_token_iterator over sub-expression index lists. tests/boost_regex.rs compiles every pattern with the facade and requires the same compile outcome (a refusal where Boost refuses), the same mark count, and byte-identical output for every match, group span, named lookup and token. Which patterns Boost compiles but the facade refuses with Error::Unsupported, their categories and the number of compared cases are derived on the oracle side by ../oracle/boost-regex/refusals.py, which re-implements the refusal rules of docs/BOOST_REGEX_SUPPORT.md independently of the Rust translator and combines them with Boost's compile outcomes; the test asserts its output exactly (probe patterns outside FUZZ one by one, the whole corpus by category, and the compared-case count).
evidence_tier: Tier 1 (executed differential, Boost.Regex 1.92) for boost_differential_corpus_has_no_mismatch; tier 1 (Boost answers transcribed from the oracle output) for case_insensitive_ranges_follow_boost and negated_classes_are_complemented_together; tier 3 (transcribed class-test literals) for class_test_expressions; tier 4 (Rust-only invariants and bounds) for the limit, work-bound, error, iterator and robustness tests.

reference_tools.boost: Boost 1.92.0 (BOOST_LIB_VERSION 1_92), Homebrew, header-only Boost.Regex v5 from /opt/homebrew/include
reference_tools.refusal_rules: ../oracle/boost-regex/refusals.py (python3): the documented refusal rules, applied to a corpus and Boost's output; prints EXPECTED_UNSUPPORTED, EXPECTED_REFUSALS, EXPECTED_CASES and the per-family counts
reference_tools.engine_crate: fancy-regex =0.19.2 (features std, unicode, perf) on regex-automata 0.4.18 and regex-syntax 0.8.11, as pinned in Cargo.lock

corpus.subsampling: The fixture keeps every pattern, every run except those marked full-only (extra operations on the same patterns), and every fixed input (edge, structured and source-derived); seeded random inputs are cut to a per-set prefix. gen.py writes both corpora in one deterministic pass; rerunning it in a scratch directory with a driver built there from driver.cpp reproduced both corpora and both Boost outputs byte for byte.
corpus.full_corpus_result: 1,402,806 cases compared, 0 mismatches, 0 compile-outcome or mark-count differences; refusals.py and the facade agree on all 347 refusals and their categories

external_reference_note: The Boost.Regex oracle driver, the corpus generator, the build script, the refusal-rule derivation and the full measurement corpus live outside this repository under ../oracle/boost-regex/ so that no C++ is committed here. Only the generated subsample and Boost's output for it are fixtures; the sha256 values above are the evidence chain for them, for the test's expected refusals and case count, and for the full-corpus run recorded in docs/BOOST_REGEX_SUPPORT.md. They are recorded, not re-verified by the in-repo gate, because they are intentionally absent from the crate. The work-bound, memory and speed measurements in the support document were taken with scratch harnesses that include src/concept/boost_regex.rs verbatim (release build, aarch64 macOS) and Boost 1.92 on the same haystacks.
